title: Precision threshold autotune for canary safeguards
creator: Alex Kim
description:
Problem: Current rollback rules rely on fixed thresholds (e.g., latency > 250ms or error rate > 0.5%) which are brittle across models, sequence length distributions, and customer workloads. This causes noisy rollbacks during traffic spikes and missed regressions when baselines differ by customer.

Goal: Implement a multimetric, autotuning rollback trigger for staged rollouts (canary, A/B, and shadow) that: (1) computes adaptive thresholds per model and route using rolling baselines, (2) composes signals (latency, error rate, token cost, throughput) with configurable weightings, (3) applies hysteresis/grace windows to avoid flapping, and (4) exposes controls in Console and API for engineers and SREs.

Approach:
- Baseline generation: maintain rolling percentiles (p50/p90/p99) per route/model for key SLO signals; support per-customer baselines where tenant-specific behavior diverges. Baselines decay using an exponential window to adapt to long-term shifts.
- Threshold autotune: thresholds are computed as baseline * (1 + delta) for latency and cost, and baseline + delta for error rate; delta is derived from configurable confidence (z-score) and observed variability (rolling stddev).
- Multimetric composition: create a composite degradation score by normalizing each metric against its autotuned threshold and applying weights. Composite score crosses a hard stop or progressive bands that trigger actions (traffic reduction, soft rollback, full rollback).
- Grace and hysteresis: require sustained breach for a configurable grace window (default 3 minutes) and require resolution for sustained healthy period before clearing. Provide max rollback rate (eg. cut 20% of traffic per step) and rate-limited rollback attempts to prevent cascading failures.
- Shadow traffic: shadow traffic results are collected and used for baseline comparisons but do not feed into production SLO counters unless explicitly promoted.
- Canary/A-B routing integration: provide hooks so rollout controller can decrement canary allocation progressively when composite score > warning and fully when > critical.
- Simulation and dry-run: implement a simulator to run historical traces and synthetic regressions against the autotune logic; dry-run mode logs suggested actions without acting.

Non-goals: replace manual release policies entirely; this is a protective layer that augments existing rollout rules and runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Autotune computes adaptive thresholds for latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput for a given model/route and stores them in metrics backend (TSDB) every minute.
Composite degradation score is emitted as a single timeseries and visible in Console with p50/p90 for canary traffic slices.
Rollout controller responds to composite score crossing "critical" by initiating a configurable rollback action (traffic cut + model swap) in staging and then in canary when enabled.
Grace window and hysteresis parameters are configurable per-project via API and are honored by the controller; flapping is prevented in simulation and live canary runs.
Dry-run mode produces identical composite scores and suggested actions in logs and Console without changing traffic allocation.

Automated rollback implementation has unit and integration tests covering edge cases (sudden burst, slow drift, noisy telemetry) and a canary run on internal traffic demonstrating no false-positive rollbacks at default config.
Runbook and Console docs updated with settings, example thresholds, and how to interpret composite score bands.
Security review completed (data used for baselining does not leak PII), and telemetry retention aligns with compliance policy.

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive autotune may rollback healthy variants during transient spikes. Mitigation: conservative default deltas, longish grace windows, dry-run by default, and require manual approval for cross-tenant rollbacks.
Risk: Per-tenant baselining increases cardinality and storage cost. Mitigation: tiered baselining (global, region, tenant-top-10) and sampling for low-volume tenants.
Risk: Composite score masks individual metric visibility. Mitigation: Console will show per-metric contributions and allow single-metric gating overrides.
Risk: Rollback actions can cascade across dependent routes. Mitigation: implement dependency awareness and a max-global-rollback-rate limiter.
